formato: Express mission · sample class · English B2
descripcion: Definición en 23 palabras puesta a prueba por un examinador kantiano; después, decálogo personal.
lead: Today you will build, in pairs, a 23-word definition of deontology. Then each of you will write your own professional decalogue: ten rules to live by at work.
leadSimple: 1. En pareja escriben qué es la deontología en 23 palabras. 2. Cada quien escribe 10 reglas para su vida profesional.

regla.titulo: Golden rule: the definition and the decalogue are yours.
regla.texto: Write them without AI. What is assessed is your reasoning, not a generated text.
regla.textoSimple: Primero escriben ustedes, sin IA. Escriban en inglés.

ficticio: All cases and situations are fictional, built for this exercise. There is no single “correct” definition: what is assessed is how you build it and how you defend it.

pasos.intro: Six situations. Nobody can see you and nobody will ever find out. Choose what you would do in each one, then compare with your partner: would you still do it if everyone in the world did the same?
pasos.introSimple: 6 situaciones. Nadie te ve. Marca qué harías. Luego comparen en pareja.

recursos.html: “Act as if your action were to become a universal law.” Do your decisions pass that test?

campos.label: A. You find a wallet on public transport, with cash and an ID card inside. Today you only have enough money for lunch or for your bus fare home.
opciones: I take my fare and return the rest
campos.labelSimple: A. Encuentras una cartera con dinero. Solo tienes dinero para comer o para el camión.

campos.label: B. You see your friend copying exam answers from WhatsApp just before handing in the paper.
campos.labelSimple: B. Tu amigo copia en el examen con WhatsApp.

campos.label: C. At a shop, the cashier gives you 200 pesos too much in change, and you have already left.
opciones: I go back and return it
I keep it: it was their mistake
campos.labelSimple: C. En la tienda te dan 200 pesos de más.

campos.label: D. Your team asks you to sign that you checked a report you have not read, because the deadline is in one hour.
opciones: I don't sign until I read it
I sign and read it later
campos.labelSimple: D. Tu equipo te pide firmar un reporte que no leíste.

campos.label: E. You could hand in an assignment written entirely by AI, and the teacher would never notice.
opciones: I hand it in as it is
I use AI only to check my work
campos.labelSimple: E. Puedes entregar una tarea hecha toda con IA. El profesor no lo sabría.

campos.label: F. Your boss asks you to tell a client that the product is ready, although it still has faults.
opciones: I say it: it's an order
I tell the client the truth
I talk to my boss first
campos.labelSimple: F. Tu jefe te pide mentir a un cliente: decir que el producto está listo.

campos.label: In which of the six would your answer not work as a law for everyone?
campos.hint: Write the letter and one line explaining why.
campos.labelSimple: ¿Cuál de tus 6 respuestas no sería buena si todos hicieran lo mismo?

pasos.intro: Use the key words as building blocks. You can use all of them or only some, but the definition must sound like you, not like a dictionary.
pasos.introSimple: Usen estas palabras para explicar qué es la deontología. Máximo 26 palabras.

claves.glosa: What I must do, even when it is not convenient.
A rule that binds everyone equally.
Treating a person as an end, never only as a means.
Reason, not taste, decides what is right.
The bond that ties me to doing my duty.

pasos.cita:
“Duty is the necessity of an action from respect for the law.”
Kant, Grounding for the Metaphysics of Morals (1785/1993)

campos.label: Pair members
campos.hint: Both names. Each of you also writes your own name at the top of the page in order to send.

pasos.titulo: The examiner of the universal law
pasos.intro: The AI will act as a Kantian examiner: it will test your definition against concrete cases. Four rounds at most.
pasos.introSimple: La IA hace preguntas difíciles sobre su definición. Respondan con razones.

voces.texto: Apply your definition to the wallet and the exam, and look for gaps.
Write the definition for you or tell you which one is correct.

pasos.aviso: In the third round the examiner will bring in Levinas's critique: universal rules may ignore the suffering of a real person. That is when you decide whether to adjust your definition.
pasos.gateTexto: Complete Phase 1 (a definition of 20 to 26 words) to unlock the examination.
prompt: Act as a Kantian examiner in a university Professional Ethics class taught in English. We are a pair of students with an upper-intermediate (B2) level of English.
At the end of this message is the definition of deontology that we wrote without AI, in 20 to 26 words.
FORMAT: write in clear B2-level English, in short paragraphs, with one question per round. Do not use audio. If we make language mistakes, do not correct them unless they change the meaning.

1. Start by saying, in one sentence, which central idea you recognise in our definition. Then ask us how, using that definition, we would solve this case: we find a wallet with cash and an ID, nobody saw us, and we do not have enough money for lunch.
2. In the second round, apply the test of the categorical imperative: ask us whether our definition distinguishes between acting from duty and acting out of convenience or fear of being caught.

3. In the third round, present Emmanuel Levinas's critique: ethics begins with responsibility before the face of the Other, and a universal rule may ignore the suffering of a real person. Ask us whether our definition leaves room for that person.

4. In the fourth round, ask us to rewrite the definition in 23 words (20 to 26 are accepted). Do not write it for us, do not suggest phrases or words to complete it, and do not say which version is correct.
5. Finish by asking which word of our definition changed the most, and why.

pasos.intro: Individual work. Use the guiding questions as a starting point: you don't need to answer them all; they are there to help you find your rules. When you finish, send your work.
pasos.introSimple: Solo. Lee las preguntas y escribe 10 reglas. Después envía.

recursos.html: What do I owe the people who receive my work, even when nobody is supervising me? What would I always do, even if it cost me time or money?
If every professional in my field followed this rule, would the world work better, or would it become impossible?
Which value would I never negotiate, not even with my boss or a client? What would I never do, even if it were legal?
What kind of professional do I want to be in ten years? Which rule helps me get there without stepping on anyone?
Who could my rule hurt if I apply it without looking at the real person in front of me?

campos.label: My personal decalogue
campos.hint: Ten short rules, each starting with a verb: “Always…”, “Never…”, “I acknowledge…”.

campos.label: The rule in my decalogue that would be hardest for me to keep, and why
campos.labelSimple: La regla más difícil para mí y por qué

rubrica.titulo: How it is assessed · 4 criteria, 16 points
filas: Combines duty, universality and respect in 20 to 26 words of your own, without copying Kant's quote.
Applies the definition to a concrete case and tells duty apart from convenience.
Responds to Levinas's critique and justifies whether the definition changes or stays the same.
Ten actionable rules, consistent with the definition and with your future professional practice.
rubrica.nota: Conversion to a final grade follows the institutional programme.

ia.titulo: How it is assessed · 4 criteria, 16 points
filas: Combines duty, universality and respect in 20 to 26 words of your own, without copying Kant's quote.
Identifies, in the opening, one of your own decisions that would not hold as a law for everyone, and explains why.
Ten actionable rules, written as duties rather than wishes, linked to your future professional practice.
The rules are consistent with your definition, and you honestly recognise which one would be hardest to keep.
ia.nota: Conversion to a final grade follows the institutional programme.
